title: Nature Travel in Meghalaya
seoTitle: Nature Travel in Meghalaya: Root Bridges, Falls, Caves
metaDescription: Nature travel in Meghalaya: living root bridges, Sohra's waterfalls, Dawki's clear river, caves, sacred groves and Laitlum, with seasons and village etiquette.
description: A guide to nature travel in Meghalaya: the living root bridges of Nongriat and Mawlynnong, the waterfalls and caves around Sohra (Cherrapunji), the clear Umngot river at Dawki, the Laitlum canyons, the Mawphlang sacred grove, the Jaintia hills' Krang Suri falls and the caves of the Garo hills, with seasons, village fees and practical tips.
dek: Meghalaya's rain-soaked plateau is cut by gorges and waterfalls, crossed by bridges grown from living roots, and cared for by its villages.

hero.alt: A boat on the clear Umngot river at Dawki, Meghalaya

intro: Meghalaya is a plateau of the Khasi, Jaintia and Garo hills. Its southern edge drops steeply to the plains of Bangladesh, and moisture-laden monsoon winds hitting that wall make the Sohra and Mawsynram area one of the wettest places on earth. The result is a landscape of deep gorges, plunging waterfalls, limestone caves and dense forest.

Much of the land belongs to clans and villages rather than the state. Many viewpoints, root bridges and falls charge a small entry fee and set their own rules, and homestays are the best way to stay close to them.
quickAnswer: The best places for nature travel in Meghalaya are the living root bridges at Nongriat and near Mawlynnong, the waterfalls and caves around Sohra (Cherrapunji), the clear Umngot river at Dawki and Shnongpdeng, the Laitlum canyons, the Mawphlang sacred grove, Krang Suri falls in the Jaintia hills and Siju cave in the Garo hills. October to April is best for clear water and walks; June to September brings the biggest waterfalls.
takeaways: Indian visitors do not need an Inner Line Permit for Meghalaya; check for any new tourist registration rules.
Sohra and Mawsynram are among the wettest places on earth; the monsoon is spectacular but very wet.
The Umngot at Dawki is clearest from roughly November to April.
The living root bridges are on UNESCO's Tentative List; India submitted the nomination dossier in January 2026.
Village fees and rules apply at most sites; carry cash.

sections.heading: Meghalaya's nature highlights at a glance
Living root bridges

items.name: Nongriat
body: The double-decker bridge at Nongriat is reached by a steep walk of a few thousand steps down from Tyrna, near Sohra. Rainbow Falls is a further walk beyond it. Most people stay a night in the village.

image.alt: The double-decker living root bridge at Nongriat
image.caption: Nongriat's double-decker bridge

items.name: Riwai, near Mawlynnong
body: A shorter walk to a single root bridge, often combined with Mawlynnong village.

image.alt: The living root bridge near Mawlynnong
image.caption: Riwai root bridge

after: Khasi communities train the aerial roots of rubber fig trees across streams over many years, and families maintain them over generations. They are called Jingkieng Jri locally and were added to UNESCO's Tentative List in 2022.

sections.heading: Sohra: waterfalls and caves
paras: The Sohra (Cherrapunji) plateau ends in cliffs, and waterfalls pour off them in the monsoon. Nohkalikai, the Seven Sisters (Nohsngithiang) and Dainthlen are the best known. Mawsmai cave is a short, lit limestone cave near the town. In the dry months many smaller falls shrink to a trickle.

sections.heading: Clear rivers: Dawki and Shnongpdeng
paras: The Umngot river at Dawki, on the Bangladesh border, is famous for water so clear that boats seem to float on air. That clarity comes in the dry season, roughly November to April; in the monsoon the river turns brown and boating may stop. Shnongpdeng, a little upstream, is quieter, with camping and swimming in calm stretches under local supervision.

sections.heading: Sacred groves and forests
paras: Sacred groves, called law kyntang in Khasi, are forests protected by communities for religious reasons. Mawphlang, about an hour from Shillong, is the best known and can be visited with a local guide; nothing may be removed from it. In the Garo hills, Balpakram National Park protects a canyon and plateau.

items.name: Krang Suri
body: A waterfall with blue pools in the Jaintia hills, near Jowai.

items.name: Siju cave
body: A long limestone cave on the Simsang river in the Garo hills; only the first section is open to casual visitors.

sections.heading: Village etiquette
list: Pay the entry or guide fee each village sets; it funds upkeep.
Ask before photographing people and follow rules at sacred sites.
Carry back all plastic; several villages ban it outright.
Do not carve, pull or hang on root bridge roots.

sections.heading: When to go
paras: October to April brings clear skies, walkable trails and the clearest rivers. The monsoon (June to September) is when the waterfalls are most dramatic, but visibility at viewpoints can be poor for days and landslides close roads. Spring brings orchids and rhododendrons in parts of the hills.

safety: The walk to Nongriat is steep; allow time and carry water.
Swim only where local operators allow it, and never in fast water after rain.
Stay on marked trails and viewpoints, and heed local closures after heavy rain.
Permits, entry rules, seasonal closures and timings change; check official sources before you go.
Carry your waste back, avoid loud music and never feed wildlife.

faqs.q: What is Meghalaya famous for in nature?
faqs.a: Living root bridges, waterfalls, caves, clear rivers and very high rainfall.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Meghalaya?
faqs.a: October to April for walks and clear rivers; June to September for waterfalls.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for Meghalaya?
faqs.a: Indian visitors do not need an Inner Line Permit. Check for any new tourist registration rules before you go.

faqs.q: How hard is the Nongriat walk?
faqs.a: It is steep, with a few thousand steps down and back up. Most reasonably fit people manage it with rest stops.

faqs.q: When is the Dawki river clearest?
faqs.a: Roughly November to April. It turns muddy in the monsoon.

faqs.q: How many days do I need in Meghalaya?
faqs.a: Five to seven days covers Shillong, Sohra, Nongriat, Mawlynnong and Dawki.
